subject: RCommander, LessR, or other user-friendly interfaces?

messages.author: 93841b2a2283ece9
messages.subject: RCommander, LessR, or other user-friendly interfaces?
parts:
Hello DRUG,

I've never used any GUIs with R (except RStudio) and I wonder about the pros and cons of RCommander, LessR, or perhaps others that I haven't heard of. Does anyone have any experience to share for novice R users? Are they able to handle material like what is covered in PLS 205 (CRDs, RCBDs, split plot designs, mixed models)? Do they have options for dealing with missing data?

Thanks for any advice out there!

Lauren

messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: RCommander, LessR, or other user-friendly interfaces?
parts:
I'm not a fan of RCommander - it's big selling point is a menu-based system instead of command-line access, which is not so helpful for code portability, and I think using menus instead of writing code hinders your ability to learn to do more complex things in R. RStudio is ok, but I'm not a big fan of the 4-way window split - it's too small on my laptop.

After trying a bunch of different thing, I ended up just using notepad++ since it has very nice R code highlighting and then copy/paste to the base R GUI. I use geany on linux.   Haven't tried LessR.

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: RCommander, LessR, or other user-friendly interfaces?
parts:
I'm personally not a big fan of RStudio, although I do think it's an
appropriate tool for beginners.

In particular, the window split IS annoying. But there's a redeeming
feature: when I do use RStudio, I edit (vim or emacs) the file in a
window outside of RStudio. If I make a change in the file in the
external window, RStudio will sense the change and use the updated
file as soon as I put the focus into the source-code window in
RStudio. Sort of the best of both worlds, although you DO have to
remember to save the file, etc.

-- Mike

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: RCommander, LessR, or other user-friendly interfaces?
parts:
I mostly use vim with vim-R-plugin, and many R developers like
Emacs+ESS (Emacs Speaks Statistics). I wouldn't recommend either
unless you already use one of those text editors. In classroom
settings in particular I always find it nice to use whatever most
other people are using.

I'm a bit confused about the concerns regarding the RStudio window
splits -- I agree the default layout is inadequate for small screens
but it is easily customized. I usually find it best to just collapse
the two left panels. Clicking "zoom" on the plot panel before
collapsing it will make sure plots open up in a new window. It's also
helpful to shrink either the console screen or text editing screen.
Admittedly I've found it tricky to drag those window resize bars on
very small screens like my phone.
